verdict.rationale: incident.io's marketing page explicitly says it offers 'public and private Status Pages' for communicating during incidents, so private status pages are a first-party capability. That single marketing line is the only evidence; there is no documentation of how access is controlled or how audiences are segmented. 'Private incidents' on the pricing page is a different feature and is not credited here. Missing for 10: documented access-control mechanisms (SSO, allowlists, authentication), customer-specific versus employee-only audience configuration, in-depth first-party docs on private or internal pages, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
